_instructions: All characters in a single characters array. Fields vary by role. Required for all: name, role, age, pronouns, physical_description, dialogue_style. See role-specific notes below.

characters.name: Full name
characters.physical_description: Appearance and bearing — specific enough to be a writing tool, not a catalog
characters.personality: Who they are: temperament, social ease, wounds, comedy, what makes them dangerous or compelling
characters.dialogue_style: First person [tense]. How they sound: register, wit level, what they reach for under pressure, what they avoid saying directly
characters.backstory: What happened before page one that shapes every choice they make in the story
characters.want: What they consciously pursue — specific and external
characters.need: What they actually lack — often the opposite of their armor
characters.flaw: The specific way their armor costs them things they want
characters.chemistry_with_protagonist: How they read each other — what the other does that gets through the armor, what they find impossible to dismiss
characters.romantic_obstacles: What stands between them — structural, informational, emotional
characters.shared_history: What they have in common before or at the story's start
characters.internal_monologue: How their POV voice sounds in the reader's head: what it notices, what it jokes about, what it goes quiet about, where it lives in the body
characters.relationship_dynamics: Per named relationship: how they read this person, what they want from them, what they won't say

characters.name: Full name
characters.motivations: What they actually want and why it makes sense to them
characters.methods: How they operate — the specific tools and tactics
characters.power_resources: What they control: money, information, relationships, leverage
characters.relationship_to_protagonist: How they relate to each protagonist — what each one means to their plans

characters.name: Full name
characters.personality: Who they are in the story's world
characters.skills_or_resources: What they bring: access, information, money, social capital
characters.role_in_story: What narrative function they serve — what they enable, block, or reveal
characters.relationship_to_protagonist: How they relate to the protagonists
